text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'eu-west-1-gpu-pool' queue > 95% for 6m, autoscaler failing to add nodes (HPA metrics missing). Paging oncall SRE.

mira: taking pager. looking at queues now.

danny: I see continuous growth on ml-inference-queue across multiple regions but eu-west is worst. Dashboard shows token backlog increasing and a spike in `pod_cpu` throttling.

mira: prom shows no recent custom metrics from prometheus-adapter to the HPA for the GPU HPA target. queries to `kubelet_custom/gpu_request` return 503 from metrics-proxy.

infra-bot: deploy-bot noticed metrics-proxy restarted 3x in last 10m: imagePullBackOff -> CrashLoopBackOff -> OOMKill.

kevin: hmm we had a recent config bump to the proxy (shorter scrape timeout). rolling it back now. `kubectl set image deployment/metrics-proxy metrics-proxy=redwood/metrics-proxy:v1.9.2 --record`

alice: rolling back to v1.9.1 and increasing scrape_timeout to 60s in configmap. applying:

```
kubectl apply -f prometheus-proxy-config.yaml
# config: scrape_timeout: 60s
```

mira: metrics proxy pod is coming up but adapter still returns 502 for the HPA queries. `kubectl logs` show `timeout waiting for remote scrape: backlog 120s`

danny: prometheus itself is under heavy backlog. retention job backfill started and is saturating TSDB WAL ingestion. That backfill is from a long-running export job kicked earlier.

mira: efforts split: infra team to stop backfill, ops to restore adapter, runtime to soft-scale to reduce customer impact.

kevin: paused backfill job: `promtool stop-backfill --id=bf-2026-03-15-03` — confirmed stopped. WAL ingest falling.

infra-bot: prometheus WAL queue depth dropping from 95% -> 40% over 2m.

mira: adapter health checks now passing. HPA queries return metrics, but HPA hasn't autoscaled because controller missed ~8 minutes of data; HPA target evaluation shows stale timestamp.

eng-runtime: we should avoid waiting for HPA to catch up. manually scaling the GPU pool to relieve queue.

alice: manual scale request issued: `redwoodctl capacity increase --pool eu-west-1-gpu-pool --gpus 8 --reason "live mitigation - autoscale lag"` — provisioning started.

danny: while nodes come up, enable temporary request-level throttling on the inference ingress to protect critical customers. Applying rate limit rules for anonymous/free-plan.

cust-sre: confirming customer impact: we have elevated latency for Dedicated customers in eu-west-1 — some 503s for large batched requests. Noticing increased reclamation errors on a few requests.

mira: quick check: error rate for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 peaked at 18% 503s, now down to 6% after throttle and partial scaling. Still above baseline.

kevin: new nodes are provisioning, kube-scheduler placing pods. GPU utilization per node currently 88% but queue length coming down.

infra-bot: autoscaler controller reports: 'metrics restored, resuming scale decisions', HPA will reconcile on next cycle (~30s).

mira: live mitigation summary (for postmortem):
- stop prometheus backfill job
- rollback metrics-proxy to v1.9.1 and increase timeout
- manual capacity increase + temporary ingress throttling
- notify customers and SRE oncall

alice: sending customer comms draft to #support: "We're mitigating an inference capacity issue in eu-west-1 affecting dedicated customers; we've increased capacity and applied temporary rate limits. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." :email:

danny: monitoring queue -> dropping steadily. will keep thread open until error rate back to baseline for 15m.

cust-sre: added affected accounts to incident tracker, contacting top-tier customers now.

eng-runtime: FYI, need a followup to remove throttles and deprovision extra capacity once HPA stable. Create a cleanup ticket.

mira: assigning post-incident actions: investigate why backfill wasn't rate-limited and why metrics-proxy OOM'd under WAL pressure; include alerting improvements for HPA stale-metrics detection.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged. If error rate < 1% and queue < 20 for 15m, please mark resolved.

mira: acknowledged. continuing to monitor.
